0.content:
Kaveh met Alhaitham, two years his junior, in the House of Daena, when he went to ask a solitary Haravatat student whether he needed help. They became close friends and research partners on a study of King Deshret's ruins. The partnership broke when Kaveh kept carrying struggling classmates and Alhaitham called his idealism a flight from reality driven by guilt. Kaveh declared he regretted ever befriending him. Years later Alhaitham found him broke at Lambad's Tavern and asked how realising his ideals had gone. Kaveh now lives in Alhaitham's house, which was converted from their old project's research site, pays rent and does all the chores. Their arguments are public, constant and mostly won by Alhaitham.

Kaveh says Alhaitham has "too big a personality" rather than none, and that the universe seems to be pranking them both. He wishes he could thank him as he did in their student days but won't give him the satisfaction. Alhaitham calls Kaveh a light of Kshahrewar and a genius whose values do not match his abilities, and quietly fetched him the Championship documents on Sachin. In Kaveh's Hangout Event Alhaitham observes that Kaveh holds others' feelings above his own. In Pride and Prejudice (3.4) Kaveh begged the Traveler not to reveal he lived there and scolded Alhaitham about his ugly new wood carving.

In 6.6 they co-led the Aaru renovation: Kaveh handled the mechanisms and materials, Alhaitham the inscriptions and strategy. On the eve of the operation Kaveh admitted he was nervous, asked whether the Azar affair had felt like this, and was told he had shown real responsibility as a citizen. He sighed that his junior acts more like the senior. Afterwards he scolded Alhaitham for not caring about their wrecked home, then quietly repaired Alhaitham's damaged collectible books. Neither describes the relationship as romantic; keep it a friendship and rivalry.

1.comment: Kaveh: The Palace of Alcazarzaray and Dori's Debt
1.content:
Dori, trading as Lord Sangemah Bay, wanted a large, extravagant mansion in a secluded spot and gave Kaveh free rein on style. He talked her into a garden of carefully chosen flowers (with Tighnari's advice) and a clifftop site in the northern mountains. At 70 percent completion the Withering wiped it out overnight. He sold his family home, added his savings and covered 70 percent of the rebuild himself. The finished palace atop a great tree is called his magnum opus. He did not earn a single Mora from it and remains in debt to Dori, who reminds him whenever payment is due.

Dori claims she secretly lent him "a LOT of Mora" and that he owes her his success. She saw at once that he was paying for his ideals, not for her. Kaveh calls her shrewd and coercive but not bad at heart. In his Hangout Event she tricked him into waiving his fee for her desert education complex, then paid for dinner. He apologised for calling her money-obsessed and promised to repay her soon.

2.comment: Kaveh: Kaveh's Father and the Interdarshan Championship
2.content:
About twenty years before 3.6, young Kaveh saw posters for the Interdarshan Championship and said how much he liked the prize, the Diadem of Knowledge. His father, an Rtawahist scholar, laughed and promised to win it so Kaveh could play with it. He was the favourite but lost, came home depressed, joined a desert research expedition and never returned; word came that he died in quicksand. Kaveh has lived with the belief that one sentence from him destroyed his family. A sketchbook page hidden with glue shows a figure sinking in sand with an apology to his father.

In 3.6, after claiming the same Diadem, Kaveh felt Sachin's despair pour into his mind, and with Alhaitham he worked out that his father had probably been shaken by Sachin's research. He went into the desert to help people who were suffering, aided Aaru Village and died saving a caravan from quicksand. Kaveh accepts this but still says it all began with his request.

His father taught him to make fatteh and was loved for his kindness; his mother said life beside him made her happy. He had begun a letter to Kaveh, but it was lost in the desert years ago.

3.content:
Mehrak is the green-and-white suitcase Kaveh built around a machine core from King Deshret's civilization, bought in the desert with every Mora he had on him. It hovers, carries his tools, surveys and maps sites, projects and sketches designs, grips his claymore in battle, and answers in beeps. Its name is an ancient word meaning "little light", and he hopes it can truly understand him. It understands only simple commands; he maintains it weekly and fusses over it like family.

It failed to keep desert foxes away in the 3.6 Championship, ran off to fetch coffee during Sabzeruz (5.1, limited), and by 2026 roams the streets alone, coming home with gifts and errands from Cyrus, Katayoun and the Treasures Street vendors.

In the 6.1 desert expedition (limited event) it led the way through the ruins, and Thoth, the Ibis King, recognised it as something King Deshret had been fond of and praised its new name. In 6.6 Heryshaf identified it as King Deshret's favourite Primal Construct.

4.content:
Faranak was a brilliant, perfectionist Kshahrewar architect and Professor Zaha Hadi's student. She was beautiful, reserved and awkward with people. She raised Kaveh among block puzzles and blueprints and wrote a book called "Architectural Drawing Basics". After her husband's death she never smiled again and could not draw. When Kaveh entered the Akademiya she took a job in Fontaine, later remarried there, and left him her Sumeru property. He attended the small wedding, glad to see her smile, then came home to an unbearably empty house. They have had little contact since, and he defends her choice.

When young Kaveh slipped his own lopsided blueprint among hers, she handed it to a client by mistake. She apologised to the client and then patiently taught her son how to draw properly. In his Hangout Event Kaveh opened her locked diary with the password "companionship". Her last entry, addressed to him, warned that a talented artist suffers and urged him to find friends to share his life with.

5.content:
Tighnari helped him choose plants for the palace and introduced him to his best friend Cyno, who to Kaveh's shock was the intimidating General Mahamatra. The group meets for meals at Tighnari's. Kaveh rants about his roommate while Collei and Tighnari try not to laugh, and he advises bringing beer to survive Cyno's jokes. Tighnari once forgave him for the mess his building over a Withering zone caused the Forest Rangers. He smells drink on Kaveh at once and invites him to dinners. Kaveh is the eldest and feels he should look responsible, though he admits he rarely repays their kindness.

At a dinner celebrating Collei's studies he argued she should join Kshahrewar and threatened to write "DON'T BECOME AN ARCHITECT" in Alhaitham's careers guide. In 4.6 he and Alhaitham traced a threat letter to the Temple of Silence and joined the search for Cyno and Cyrus. In 6.6 he told Cyno and Tighnari to take no risks before splitting up.

6.comment: Kaveh: Sachin and the Diadem of Knowledge
6.content:
During the limited-time 3.6 Akademiya Extravaganza, Kaveh entered the Interdarshan Championship for Kshahrewar to win the prize money and buy a house of his own. He chased Swiftflies with Faruzan's mechanical butterflies, fainted in the desert after leading lost foxes to safety, and finally claimed the Diadem of Knowledge. A fragment of the long-dead scholar Sachin spoke in his mind. Sachin believed human nature breeds only conflict and wanted Kaveh, an idealistic genius like himself, to inherit his fortune and continue his research. Kaveh destroyed the Diadem, gave the estate to people in need, and accepted that silencing Sachin's views was a responsibility he would bear. Nahida sealed the research away.

He won the Championship anyway. The remaining prize was a limited-edition card, which he sold to Cyno for one million Mora. He used it to pay the month's debts and treat everyone to dinner, and was annoyed that Alhaitham skipped it. Alhaitham's note on Sachin read that lofty ideals may be no defence against nihilism but little decisions might be. Kaveh quoted it to himself on the eve of the 6.6 operation.

7.comment: Kaveh: The Withering and the First Palace
7.content: The Withering spread unusually fast the year Kaveh built Dori's mansion. On a quiet night it consumed the 70-percent-finished palace. The Forest Rangers dispersed it, but nothing could be saved, and Dori demanded he leave the project. Kaveh begged to finish it and spent the night on the ruins deciding that his empty family home was just a building, not a home, before selling it at sunrise. Alhaitham notes the mess was a real headache for the Rangers.

8.comment: Kaveh: Lambad's Tavern and the Bulletin Boards
8.content: After the bankruptcy Kaveh drank at Lambad's Tavern for over a fortnight, passing out at the table. Lambad kept a seat and a few free drinks for him, and Kaveh repaid him by redesigning the second-floor booths. Lambad remarks that Kaveh vows to drink till he is carried out "every other day". Kaveh and Alhaitham also carry on their quarrels in writing on the Mahamata, Puspa Cafe and Port Ormos bulletin boards. Kaveh writes his while drunk, forgets them, and privately hopes Alhaitham never finds out.

9.comment: Kaveh: Port Ormos and the Pharos Lighthouse
9.content: Kaveh's early career centred on Port Ormos. He renovated the landmark lighthouse's weathered exterior, though its eroded foundation could only partly be saved. He modified the port's elevators and cargo-handling structures and designed the arch bridge, splitting the port into two levels modelled on nearby tree growth. It is the project he brags about most after the palace. The work went smoothly with no recorded complaints, but a tight budget forced cheaper timber than he wanted. Seeing his idea become a lasting part of the world taught him that a building's worth is judged by generations of people.

10.content:
In 6.6 something blocked Irminsul from within, Nahida collapsed holding back the damage, Sumeru City was evacuated and a barrier sealed the nation. Kaveh joined the scholars at Caravan Ribat and the Temple of Silence. He and Alhaitham proposed restarting the Akasha through King Deshret's machine Aaru, and with the consent of the Seven Pillars they took over Aaru's mainframe in the Mausoleum. He apologised to Bennu for Alhaitham's bluntness, presented a rough draft proposal and joked about turning around five drafts in a day. When the plan changed, he calculated materials for new terminals for everyone in Sumeru, including the desert folk. The merged system overloaded Irminsul, and the corrupted tree was destroyed and replaced by Aaru.

Inside Aaru he worked the Primal Embers while Alhaitham read the obelisks. He hesitated over deleting old Gurabad conflict reports in case Vahumana needed them, then agreed. He volunteered to face the dangerous chessboard trial first because he was Alhaitham's senior. Tighnari asked if he had handled big projects before; Kaveh said the palace was nothing next to this. Earlier at Caravan Ribat he haggled with Alhaitham over rent for the evacuation period and fretted that a thief might steal his conspicuously hung new scroll.

11.content: As a student Kaveh thought Visions came at moments of crisis, but none came when he dragged classmates out of a collapsing tomb. He stopped expecting one and assumed he was not a person with a strong enough wish. On the night he sold his house to rebuild the palace, he made the flatbread dish his father had taught him, shaped like a tiny Palace of Alcazarzaray. When he broke it open, a Dendro Vision lay inside. He says hopes and dreams sometimes bring suffering instead of happiness, but luckily he doesn't mind his Vision.

12.comment: Kaveh: The Pendulum of Weal and Woe (Hangout)
12.content: Kaveh's Hangout Event begins with him storming out of a meeting over a client's sixth rejected draft and drowning it at Lambad's. Depending on the Traveler's choices, he returns to the client Badawi, a former Eremite secretly funding a library for desert children in Aaru Village. Kaveh redesigns it in a leaner style named after the Traveler and, through Dori, it grows into a full education complex. Or he revisits his past: his mother's diary, his annotated books at the House of Daena, his Port Ormos bridge and a desert viewpoint where he decides that his buildings will outlast his pain. Or he takes a well-paid lecturing job from an old classmate, Alkami, and exposes it as a predatory loan scam. He tells the Traveler that guilt, not idealism, first drove his kindness, and that Alhaitham thinks all idealists drown. He also reveals that he was once scammed and ambushed in the desert by a man he tried to help.

13.content: Professor Zaha Hadi is a retired Kshahrewar authority on formal garden design and Faranak's former teacher. She lives near Cyrus, whom she accused of stealing her prize tomato in a retirees' vegetable contest. She told Kaveh he shares his mother's looks, stubbornness and awkwardness, and that few genius Kshahrewar architects ever find happiness because they fight clients for their vision. She said Faranak argued with clients almost daily until she met Kaveh's father, whose support helped her choose him over many admirers, and that true art is rarely understood. This led Kaveh to the diary password "companionship".

14.comment: Kaveh: Faruzan and the Championship rivals
14.content: In the 3.6 Championship (limited event) Kaveh and Faruzan teamed up twice, first with mechanical butterflies and then digging out a Ley Line Disruptor, and drew lots each time. She won the first draw and he the second. She had once discussed mechanism principles with him and plans to treat him to a meal "once her funding is approved". He calls her intense but genuinely expert, and notes that some say all Haravatat scholars are hard to get along with. In 6.6 she called for him repeatedly while he was too busy reviewing proposals.

15.comment: Kaveh: Thoth and the 6.1 Desert Expedition
15.content: During the limited-time 6.1 event, Kaveh and Alhaitham joined Tighnari, Cyno, Sethos, Layla and the Traveler to explore unknown desert ruins. Sethos called Kaveh "our renowned architect", and Kaveh accused Alhaitham of pulling strings at the House of Daena. Mehrak found stone slabs and led them deeper. Kaveh recognised murals of the noble Goudarz and the "Temptress of Woe" from desert history papers and worried that the "wisdom" being granted had ruined them. A talking cat revealed himself as Thoth. Kaveh apologised to the "esteemed cat", insisted Mehrak was not a "contraption", and silently congratulated himself when Thoth approved the name.

key: Reasoning Knows Not Time of Day
16.comment: Kaveh: Kaveh in Sumeru festivals and events
16.content: Limited-event appearances, canon but not widely known. Summertide Scales and Tales (4.8): while tipsy he circled a misprinted name in a House of Daena detective novel. Others then circled every name, rumours of hidden treasure spread, and the name he circled proved to be the killer; he bought the defaced book. Chromatic Ode of Candies and Roses (5.1): for Nahida's Sabzeruz birthday surprise he designed a candy tower meant to burst softly over her Flower Carriage, triggered remotely by Mehrak, and panicked when Mehrak went missing fetching coffee.

17.content: Kaveh first met the Traveler at Alhaitham's house and asked them to keep his living arrangement and bankruptcy secret. He treats them as a friend he can confide in and once asked shyly whether he could call them that. As a Teapot guest he is thrilled by a realm that is "a sketchbook that'll never run out of pages". He is horrified by careless arrangements, and prays the Traveler finds their sibling, offering to build them a home free of charge when they do. He tells them a house becomes a home only when people live in it.
